job.title: Office Manager
job.description:
Office Manager
6-Month Contract - potential to extend
Melbourne CBD
$110,000 + super FTE

About the client

Our client is a global technology organisation with a growing presence across Australia and New Zealand. Their regional offices sit within a well-established international workplace and facilities function, with strong support from regional and global leadership. They place real value on creating offices that are welcoming, inclusive and run smoothly, so their people can focus on doing great work.

About the role

Based in their Melbourne CBD office, you will be the go-to person for office operations and facilities, while also overseeing the Perth, Sydney and Auckland sites. This is a hands-on, on-site role where you will look after everything from vendors and building management to physical security, safety compliance and the local budget. You will be the face of the office for staff and visitors in this 6-month engagement, which starts quickly and may extend to 12 months.

Duties

  • Oversee day-to-day office operations across Melbourne, Perth, Sydney and Auckland, including front desk, mailroom, supplies, amenities and general upkeep.
  • Manage relationships with landlords, building management and facility vendors such as cleaning, security and catering, including tracking SLAs and KPIs.
  • Act as the local physical security point of contact, managing access control, badge and visitor management, incident response and emergency drills.
  • Manage the local operating budget, raising purchase orders, matching vendor invoices and flagging variances against forecast.
  • Partner with HR, Talent Acquisition and local leadership to prepare for new starters and coordinate office events, celebrations and culture initiatives.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in office management, workplace services or facilities management, ideally within a multinational technology or corporate environment.
  • Proven experience managing vendors and contractors, including reviewing quotes, negotiating contracts and tracking service performance.
  • Sound knowledge of building management practices and Australian workplace health and safety, fire safety and security requirements.
  • Experience managing an operating budget, purchase orders and invoice reconciliation.
  • Confidence using workplace technology such as Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom and ticketing systems like ServiceNow.
  • Comfortable overseeing multiple sites and handling executive escalations calmly and professionally.
  • Available to start quickly and work on-site in the Melbourne CBD for a 6-month contract.

How to apply

If this sounds like the right next step for you, we would love to hear from you, so please apply today.

job.title: Event Coordinator
job.description:
Event Coordinator
Chatswood Office - Hybrid working
3 month temporary contract
$40 per hour + Super

About the client

Our client is a well-established industry association based in Chatswood, delivering a busy calendar of conferences, gala dinners and webinars for its members and the wider sector. With a peak events period underway, they are bringing in extra coordinator support to keep everything running smoothly.

About the role

As Events Coordinator, you will take direction from the Senior Event Manager and Event Managers and pick up the support tasks that make events run well, from logistics and registrations to run sheets and delegate enquiries. It is an output-focused role, so you will be trusted to own delegated work, deliver it on time and spot what needs to happen next without waiting to be asked. You will also help deliver smaller, repeatable events using the team's established templates and processes. This is a 3-month contract with the opportunity to extend, and there are two positions available.

Duties

  • Coordinate venues, catering, AV, suppliers and contractors for conferences, gala dinners and webinars, including sourcing venues and obtaining quotes as directed.
  • Follow up with speakers and presenters to gather information and presentations ahead of each event.
  • Support delegate registrations in Jomablue, troubleshooting routine registration and platform issues and escalating problems where required.
  • Prepare run sheets, briefing documents, checklists and venue event orders.
  • Manage the shared events inbox and phone line, responding promptly to delegate enquiries.

Requirements

  • 2 to 3 years' experience in an events coordinator or similar events support role.
  • Hands-on experience supporting the delivery of conferences, gala dinners or webinars.
  • Experience using event registration platforms; Jomablue is highly regarded and Aventri is also valued.
  • Familiarity with HubSpot or a similar CRM.
  • Strong MS Office skills, particularly Excel for building and maintaining event trackers.
  • Availability to start soon and work from the Chatswood office at least 3 days a week.
  • Full working rights in Australia.

How to apply

If you enjoy keeping events on track and want to step into a busy team where your work makes a visible difference, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Staff Incident Response Commander
job.description:
• 12-month Sydney contract with a global software company
  • Hands-on forensics across Kubernetes, AWS and GCP
  • Senior IC role shaping process, tooling and mentoring


About the client

Our client is a global software and digital media company whose products are used by individuals and enterprises around the world. It's cyber defence centre protects the company’s products, platforms and customers, working closely with engineering, product and partner teams. The incident response team handles serious, high-visibility security events across modern cloud and application environments. It is a team that values sound judgement, composure and genuine technical depth.

About the role

This is one of the most senior incident command roles in the team, and it stays hands-on. You will lead the most complex security incidents from first alert to closure while doing the forensic investigation yourself, across web applications, APIs, containers and multi-cloud infrastructure. You will bring order to incidents that span many internal teams and external partners, and move comfortably between deep technical analysis and clear briefings for senior leadership. Beyond live incidents, you will help shape how the team responds through better process, tooling, exercises and mentoring.

Duties

  • Command complex security incidents across the full response lifecycle, coordinating internal teams, external partners and their security operations centres.
  • Personally investigate web application, API, cloud and container compromises, including credential and data-exposure scenarios.
  • Collect, preserve and analyse forensic evidence across hosts, networks, cloud platforms and large log sources, keeping defensible records throughout.
  • Brief senior leadership clearly under pressure, and assign and drive remediation across multiple teams and organisations.
  • Build tooling for evidence collection at scale, and lead retrospectives, tabletop exercises, training and mentoring for responders and commanders.


Requirements

  • Extensive front-line incident response and digital forensics experience across many major incidents, with proven command of the full incident lifecycle.
  • Hands-on investigation of web application and API compromises, such as broken access control, authentication and authorisation bypass, IDOR, API abuse and CMS exploitation.
  • Cloud-native and container forensics, including Kubernetes and ephemeral infrastructure, with strong AWS and GCP experience across logging, identity and authorisation models.
  • Deep host and network forensics, including Linux internals and Windows and macOS artefacts.
  • EDR at scale (for example CrowdStrike Falcon), complex SIEM analytics, and log and data analysis across large platforms and data warehouses.
  • Scripting in Bash and at least one interpreted language, such as Python.
  • Working knowledge of ISO 27001, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR and PCI.
  • Willingness to join an on-call rotation and respond to critical events.
  • Highly regarded: Azure, malware triage and reverse engineering, GCFA, GCIH, GNFA or cloud security certifications, and a government or law-enforcement investigation background.


How to apply

If this sounds like the kind of work you do best, we would love to hear from you, apply now.

job.title: IT Applications Administrator
job.description:
About the client

Our client is a major national cultural institution in Canberra, bringing together a world-class museum and an extensive archive. Its work helps Australians understand an important part of the nation’s story and its lasting impact on Australian society. The IT team delivers modern, secure, resilient and user-centred technology services that support daily operations, public-facing digital services and an ongoing program of enterprise transformation.

About the role

As IT Applications Administrator, you will be the technical custodian for the business applications at the heart of the institution’s collection, including its Collection Management System and Digital Asset Management System. Working under broad direction, you will keep these platforms secure, available and well supported, while driving continual improvement across integrations, databases and cloud services. You will work closely with business stakeholders, vendors and technical specialists, so your work directly shapes how the collection is managed and shared. This is a 12-month contract with potential to extend.

Duties

  • Administer, support and continuously improve a portfolio of business applications, including the Collection Management System, Digital Asset Management System and SaaS platforms.
  • Act as technical custodian for designated applications, covering vendor engagement, configuration, release management, lifecycle planning, monitoring and maintenance.
  • Manage integrations and data flows between business applications, databases, cloud services and enterprise platforms.
  • Coordinate application, database and supporting infrastructure upgrades in line with the Information Security Manual (ISM), the Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) and vendor best practice.
  • Document applications and support procedures, and develop and maintain ITSM processes covering standard changes, incident management and problem management.

Requirements

  • Proven experience administering enterprise business applications, including configuration, upgrades, troubleshooting, user support, vendor management and integration with corporate systems.
  • Experience supporting application integrations using APIs, middleware, ETL processes and scripting such as PowerShell, with database platforms including Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365, including Entra ID, Azure SQL Managed Instance, Azure Storage, Azure Monitor and Azure Key Vault.
  • Experience supporting business-critical production applications in Australian Government or another highly regulated environment, including incident, problem, change and release management, disaster recovery and business continuity.
  • Highly developed written and verbal communication skills, including preparing and maintaining complex technical and non-technical documentation.
  • Experience with museum, cultural institution or archival systems, such as Piction, MuseumPlus or equivalent CMS and DAMS platforms, is highly regarded.
  • Negative Vetting 1 security clearance (Australian citizenship required).

How to apply

If this sounds like the right next step for you, we would love to hear from you, so please apply now.

job.title: Customer Complaints and Resolutions Analyst
job.description:

Sydney | Hybrid | $40-45ph + Super | ASAP till April 30th 2027

You will play a key role in delivering fair customer outcomes while ensuring compliance with regulatory frameworks and industry standards.

Key Responsibilities

  • Investigate and resolve customer complaints across retail and wholesale insurance products
  • Prepare Internal Dispute Resolution (IDR) determinations

If this aligns with your background, apply now for immediately consideration

job.title: Operations Manager
job.description:
Operations Manager
$140k - $160k + Super (FTE)
Sydney CBD - Hybrid
PART-TIME – 3 DAYS PER WEEK
Permanent

About the client
Our client is a respected, member-based peak body in the financial services sector, based in Sydney. They advocate on behalf of their members, contribute to policy and support best practice across the industry, working with a range of government and industry stakeholders. As a small team, it's an organisation where your contribution is visible and there's real room to shape how things are done.

About the role
This is a senior, cross-functional role for an experienced operator who can work both strategically and hands-on. Working closely with the CEO and leadership team, you'll oversee operations, governance processes, budgeting, risk, HR and IT, making sure the organisation runs effectively, compliantly and sustainably. You'll have genuine scope to identify what could be done better, make recommendations to senior leaders and see change through. Offered on a permanent part-time basis, three days a week, it suits someone who wants senior-level impact with flexibility.

Duties

  • Drive operational improvement across the organisation, identifying inefficiencies and leading projects from review through to implementation, starting with travel management and a review of IT support arrangements.
  • Manage the board and committee cycle, including the annual meeting calendar, agendas, board papers, minutes and action follow-up, so the CEO and Board are well supported and informed.
  • Lead the annual budget process with the CEO and external accountant, identifying cost efficiencies and strengthening financial controls and procurement practices.
  • Maintain and strengthen governance, risk and compliance frameworks, including workplace policies, WHS requirements and risk reporting.
  • Oversee IT and information security, including cybersecurity, records management and technology platforms, and manage outsourced providers through to tender where needed.

Requirements

  • Significant experience in a senior operations or business management role spanning multiple functions, such as governance, finance, risk, HR and IT.
  • A proven track record of identifying and driving process improvements and seeing them through to implementation.
  • The judgement and confidence to make decisions independently and provide sound recommendations to senior leaders.
  • Strong planning and project management skills, with the ability to move between strategic and hands-on work.
  • A sound understanding of governance frameworks and regulatory compliance, with experience supporting a board or committees.
  • Strong financial literacy, including budgeting and reporting.

How to apply
If you're an experienced operator ready to make a real impact at a senior level, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Sales Operations Analyst
job.description:
About the client

Our client is a global enterprise software company with a well-established presence across Asia Pacific and Japan. Its portfolio spans several major business units, sold to enterprise and commercial customers around the world. The APJ business development team sits within marketing and works across the full product range, connecting marketing demand with the sales organisation. The team runs on global processes, so you will be joining a mature, well-structured sales operations function.

About the role

This is a contract role based in Sydney, supporting the APJ business development representative (BDR) organisation. You will act as the regional trusted advisor to a US-based sales operations leader and work closely with the Sydney BDR leader, who supports Australia, Japan and Singapore. Your work will shape how the team is staffed, measured and paid, from territory planning and quota attainment through to the accuracy of the CRM data behind every performance report. It suits an experienced operator who can pick up new processes quickly and take ownership of problems without step-by-step guidance.

Duties

  • Lead headcount, staffing and territory planning for the APJ BDR team, keeping territory assignments and coverage up to date.
  • Analyse BDR performance and quota attainment, covering pipeline, conversion and ramp, and turn the results into quarterly business updates and clear recommendations.
  • Own CRM data integrity in Microsoft Dynamics 365, making sure opportunity attribution and creator credit are correct so reporting and compensation are accurate.
  • Support compensation and incentive activity, including quota administration, spiffs and annual top-performer recognition.
  • Work with the sales help desk, IT and sales operations peers across the region and the US to resolve CRM and reporting issues.

Requirements

  • Proven experience in B2B sales operations or sales analysis, including forecasting, pipeline management and quota or target setting.
  • Hands-on experience with an enterprise-grade CRM, with Microsoft Dynamics 365 strongly preferred.
  • The ability to explain the drivers of sales performance, such as average deal size, pipeline metrics, conversion rates and forecasting methods.
  • Strong Excel and data analysis skills. Power BI and Databricks experience are highly regarded.
  • Confidence working independently and taking ownership of new tasks with minimal onboarding.
  • A bachelor’s degree in business, finance or a related field.
  • Availability for early-morning Sydney calls with US-based colleagues during the interview process and initial training.
  • Full Australian working rights.

How to apply

If this sounds like the next step for you, we would love to hear from you, so please apply with your CV today.

job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
Executive Assistant to the Founder and CEO
12-month Fixed-Term Contract
Eastern Suburbs- great transport links
Salary- DOE- $120-140k+super

  • Be the right hand to a globally recognised founder and CEO, a true pioneer in her field
  • 12-month parental leave cover with a real path to permanency in a growing organisation
  • Complex global diary, international travel

About the client

Our client is a fast-growing Australian technology start-up, founded and led by a globally recognised pioneer in her field. The organisation is driven by a belief that its work can change the world and a strong commitment to the greater good. It is a one-of-a-kind environment where ambition, purpose and discretion sit side by side.

About the role

You will be the trusted right hand to the Founder and CEO, supporting her through a complex, high-stakes, high-growth chapter. She travels extensively, domestically and internationally, so you will manage a complex and shifting diary across time zones and pull together detailed travel plans, including visas. You will work closely with the wider management team and play a key role in facilitating quarterly board meetings with a global Chair. This is a 12-month fixed-term contract covering parental leave, with a real possibility of converting to a permanent role for the right person. Given the nature of this business, you will be comfortable supporting high-level EA tasks and serving as a go-to person for the office. This is a true wearer of all hats role!

Duties

  • Manage a complex, constantly shifting diary across multiple time zones.
  • Plan and coordinate domestic and international travel, including itineraries, visas and logistics.
  • Facilitate and support quarterly board meetings, working closely with the US-based Chair.
  • Act as a trusted partner to the CEO, managing high-profile stakeholder relationships with discretion.
  • Work closely with the wider management team to keep priorities aligned and information flowing.

Requirements

  • Australian Citizenship; required to obtain baseline security clearance.
  • Ability to work onsite five days a week.
  • A career EA with proven experience supporting C-Suite executives at CEO level.
  • Exposure to global organisations, including complex international travel and time zone management.
  • Experience supporting board meetings is highly regarded.
  • Maturity, sound judgement and strong commercial acumen.
  • A high level of discretion when handling confidential and sensitive matters.

How to apply

If you are an experienced EA ready for a truly unique, career-defining role, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Engineer
job.description:
Senior IP Networking Engineer
Sydney – Rosebery | Onsite with free parking | Full-time permanent role

  • Senior IP networking engineer role with a genuine, longer-term path to team leadership
  • Hands-on technical role built on TCP/UDP, VLANs, multicast and PTP, Cisco a bonus
  • Sydney based, working across APAC for a global leader in broadcast and live event tech


We are working exclusively with a world-leading business whose products are used in high-end, large-scale events. Their technology is trusted on the world's biggest stages across broadcast, live events, pro-audio, sports, theatre, and security applications. And despite their global reach, they've retained a local, family feel to their operations in Sydney.

About the Role

This is a Sydney-based, senior technical role supporting APAC customers on complex IP networking issues within broadcast and live event technology, spanning TCP/UDP, VLANs, multicast and PTP. The role is genuinely hands-on: you will work directly on the trickier technical cases and act as a point of escalation, while mentoring and supporting other engineers across the APAC team.

Duties

  • Provide hands-on technical support on complex customer cases involving IP networking, including TCP/UDP, VLANs, multicast and PTP.
  • Mentor and support engineers across the APAC team, sharing technical expertise and helping resolve escalated issues.
  • Step in on sensitive customer relationship matters, such as billing disputes or SLA concerns, as they arise.
  • Build familiarity with the team's case follow-up discipline and customer engagement processes through Salesforce.
  • Travel periodically to regional offices and training events

Requirements

  • Strong, hands-on foundation in IT/IP networking, including TCP/UDP, VLANs, multicast and PTP; Cisco knowledge highly regarded.
  • Background in broadcast, pro-audio or media/OT technology.
  • A Principal Engineer, Senior Engineer or Technical Lead background, with genuine mentoring experience valued; a formal "Manager" title is not required.
  • Comfortable working within a team spread across different cultural contexts, particularly across the Asia-Pacific region, with openness to growing into people leadership over time.
  • A hands-on, proactive approach.
  • CRM experience, particularly Salesforce, is an advantage
  • Full working rights in Australia

job.title: ICT Operations and Business Manager
job.description:
ICT Operations and Business Manager (Contract)

  • Run day-to-day ICT at a major Sydney cultural institution
  • Broad remit: service, vendors, budgets, risk and procurement
  • 6-month NSW Government contract, ASAP start
  • Up to $815 + Super p/day

About the client

Our client is one of Australia's longest-established cultural and scientific institutions, based in the Sydney CBD and operating within the NSW Government. It cares for one of the country's most significant natural history and cultural collections, and delivers exhibitions, research and education programs onsite, online and across the community. Its ICT team provides level 2 and 3 support across the organisation, underpinning collection management and document management systems, a managed Virtual Private Cloud environment and an active program of cyber and digitisation work.

About the role

This is a 6-month contract for an experienced ICT operations manager to run the operational and business side of the ICT function, reporting to the Head of ICT. You will keep ICT services running, planned, governed and accountable, so the Head of ICT can focus on direction and approvals. You will lead the team day to day, manage vendors and shared services, and look after budgets, risk, compliance and procurement within NSW public-sector frameworks. Where a decision needs delegation, you will prepare the advice and recommendation for the Head of ICT to approve.

Duties

  • Manage the day-to-day delivery of ICT services, including service assurance, availability, support and maintenance, keeping level 2 and 3 support on track against agreed service levels.
  • Plan and prioritise the ICT team's work, lead and coordinate staff, and hold coaching and performance conversations, recommending people decisions to the Head of ICT.
  • Manage suppliers, managed service providers and shared-service arrangements, monitoring contract performance and resolving service issues.
  • Track ICT budgets and expenditure, produce operational and financial reporting, and prepare papers and actions for the ICT and Cyber Security Governance Committee.
  • Maintain ICT risk registers, support compliance with NSW Government cyber security and records obligations, and run ICT procurement in line with NSW procurement rules and whole-of-government arrangements.

Requirements

  • Demonstrated NSW or Australian Government experience in an ICT operations or ICT business management role, including working within public-sector accountability, decision-making and assurance processes and whole-of-government arrangements.
  • A proven track record as a general ICT operations manager across service delivery, work planning and team coordination.
  • People management experience with ICT staff, including coaching and performance conversations.
  • Hands-on experience managing vendors, managed service providers or shared services against contracts and service levels.
  • Experience with ICT budget tracking and financial reporting.
  • Working knowledge of ICT risk, compliance, governance, government procurement and cyber security good practice.
  • Comfort operating in an advisory role, preparing recommendations for approval by a more senior leader.
  • Familiarity with the NSW Cyber Security Policy, NSW procurement rules or whole-of-government ICT schemes, and experience in a cultural, research or collections-based organisation, will be highly regarded.

How to apply

If this sounds like the right next contract for you, we'd love to hear from you, so please apply now.

job.title: Field Sales Representative

job.title: Operations & Membership Officer
job.description:
Operations & Membership Officer

Chirnside Park, VIC

Full time

Interstate and occasional international travel a few times a year

Whether your background is in events, marketing, account management or B2B partnerships, this role is a chance to take your skills into a national peak industry body. You'll coordinate trade shows (with international travel), drive member growth, manage sponsor relationships and deliver marketing campaigns, with a lot of variety from one week to the next. No association experience is needed, just the energy to get stuck in.

The organisation runs industry-leading events, including a flagship triennial trade exhibition, alongside a strong member services and partnerships program. With over 150 Australian-based company members, this is a genuinely varied role working closely with the General Manager, CEO and business partners across the full operations of the association.

What you'll be doing:

  • Delivering clear, timely reporting on acquisition, sponsorship revenue, event performance and marketing engagement.
  • Proactively identifying, targeting and converting new member companies to drive satisfaction, retention and growth.
  • Coordinating the association's presence at domestic and international trade events, from stand design and staffing through to marketing and lead follow-up.
  • Building and nurturing relationships with sponsors and service partners, and pitching new partners that resonate with the membership.
  • Driving member communications across newsletters, LinkedIn, forums and other digital channels, including publications and member content.
  • Managing the association's recurring events calendar, including its flagship exhibition, an annual awards program, and other member gatherings.

What we're looking for:

  • 5+ years' experience in a customer-facing, coordination or business operations role (association, events or B2B environment preferred).
  • Marketing experience (mainly social media and EDM creation).
  • Strong relationship management and communication skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in a professional context.

Great to have (not essential):

  • Background in events coordination or trade exhibition delivery.
  • Exposure to sponsorship or partnership management.
  • Familiarity with the packaging, processing or broader manufacturing sector.

This is a fantastic opportunity for a relationship-driven operator who wants genuine variety, autonomy and the chance to play a key role in the continued success of a peak industry body.

Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience, circa $90,000 to $100,000 plus superannuation, with interstate and occasional international travel a few times a year.
